paper.title: Mathematical Models and Applications, With Emphasis on the Social, Life, and Management Sciences
paper.journal: Prentice-Hall (rumor-spread chapter; cf. Daley & Kendall, Nature 1964)

headline: Maki-Thompson rumor (well-mixed CTMC): 3/3 locked clauses REPRO; mean i_inf=0.2020 (analytic 0.2032), peak spreader=0.3106 (analytic 0.3069), rate-independence max|delta|=0.0000

verdicts.gate: P1 never-hear constant: mean i_inf in [0.195,0.211] AND |mean i_inf - 0.2032| < 0.008
P2 rate-independence: max pairwise |i_inf(rate_i)-i_inf(rate_j)| < 0.01 over rates [0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0]
P3 peak spreader in [0.29,0.32] (target 0.3069) AND |dev i_inf(N)| monotone-decreasing, N=1e5 within 0.004 of 0.2032

extra.metric: final ignorant fraction i_inf; peak spreader fraction
extra.framing: well-mixed stochastic compartment CTMC (directed pairwise contacts); disclosed hybrid, not autonomous per-agent scheduling
extra.scope: faithful reproduction of a published synthetic model (Maki-Thompson directed-contact rumor process); no real-world data; the contribution is whether the harness + discipline reproduce the rate-invariant never-hear constant (0.2032) and the peak spreader (1-ln2) and would catch an artifact

citations: Maki, D.P. & Thompson, M. (1973). Mathematical Models and Applications, With Emphasis on the Social, Life, and Management Sciences. Prentice-Hall. (directed-contact rumor model).
Daley, D.J. & Kendall, D.G. (1964). Epidemics and rumours. Nature 204:1118.
Daley, D.J. & Kendall, D.G. (1965). Stochastic rumours. J. Inst. Math. Appl. 1:42-55. (fixed point theta=exp(-(1+rho)(1-theta)); rho=1 => 0.2032).

benchmark.note: no cross-tool baseline; faithful single-implementation reproduction validated against the analytic MT fixed point theta=exp(-2(1-theta))=0.2032 and peak 1-ln2=0.3069
